Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Game End 4 Reference Overview Have the most points at the end of 9 rounds Turn First, you MAY spend one key to either move the Messenger to the other row OR discard the row the Messenger is on and refill it. After which, you MUST buy a card in the row the Messenger is on, the cost is at the top left of the card (you may have ways to discount this cost, but never below 0). If you are unable to buy a card, you MUST take any available card but flip it face down and its features are no longer applicable, but you gain 6 coin and 2 Keys. Regardless of whether the card you gained is faceup or facedown, place it into your grid orthogonally adjacent to an existing card whilst making sure not to go beyond the 3x3 boundaries. After placement, carry out the card's ability. This may affect you, all opponents, or a neighbour of your choice. The card may also instruct you to move the Messenger to a particular row. After which, refill any row with fewer than 3 cards. Game End The Game ends after the 9th round, in which all players will have a 3x3 grid. Any leftover gold can be assigned to Purses on cards up to the capacity of that Purse. Cards score based on their particular requirements. Facedown cards don't score anything. Leftover Keys are worth 1VP each. Gold not assigned to a Purse does not score anything. The player with the most points wins! If tied, the player with the most Gold not in a Purse wins! [Rating: 1/10] Published in UK by Hachette Boardgames that is owned by a far-right nationalist. Buy the Pandasaurus version from US.

[Rating: 2/10] As simple as open-drafting and tableau building gets. Would be good to introduce players to those genres, but I worry that repeated plays would start trending in the same direction.

[Rating: 2/10] Combo lottery! Another iteration of: we take from the middle and place in our area. In this case, it happens with cards in a 3x3 grid. There are lots of combos and very little interaction, unless you study the other players' cards closely the whole time and are prepared to pay to clear the display. If luck is on your side, the right card will appear when you draw again, when no one else can clear it. Ultimately, it's pure lottery which cards are currently on display. Lots of calculations for nothing!

[Rating: 3/10] It’s inoffensive, but it’s also completely recycled from other games. It does absolutely nothing unique.

[Rating: 3/10] What a poor game. Noobies are hampered by not knowing what are good/fair or poor card combinations, as with all these so called games (of fun).   And I came second out of 5 players, so not "sour grapes".  There are simply much better fillers out there - ones that are not mutli-solitaire and involve interaction with your opponents.  Oh, and the playing time is a joke. We payed with 5 and even allowing for rules explanation, it took over 100 minutes. What a waste of good game playing time.  Gets a 3 because there are actually worse games than this being sold (and played!!) - the "cult of the new

[Rating: 3/10] A fun tableau-building filler that does not really grab me. Seems like there are a million of these.  04/29/25

[Rating: 3/10] Pretty pointless game, even with only 2 players (the more you add, the more chaos you get). Take a card, get the reward and hope that fitting cards will show up when it's your turn again. That's the game.  I never liked games where you refill the card row for the next player, who may be very lucky. Sure, this is not a long game, but I still dislike it, as it happens even in a short game.  While Fantasy Realms isn't something I'm looking forward to, it's the MUCH better game where you actually need to make decisions.  The art is fun, though!
